Maximilian: German form of Latin Maximilianus, from Maximus 'greatest'. Borne by Habsburg emperors.
Tia: Spanish and Portuguese for 'aunt'. Also a short form of names ending in -tia, or Greek 'goddess'. Origin varies.
Matti: Finnish form of Matthew, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Vera: Latin 'true', or Slavic vera 'faith'. Both meanings are in use.
Maia: Greek and Roman goddess of spring; also a Pleiad. Possibly from 'mother' or 'nurse'.
Nikolas: Form of Nicholas, from Greek 'victory of the people'.
Mayra: Probably a variant of Maira or Myra. Possibly a Spanish form of Mary or Arabic 'provider'. Origin uncertain.
Lilith: Hebrew, possibly from Akkadian 'night spirit'. A figure in Jewish folklore; the first wife of Adam.
Miya: Japanese, possibly meaning 'shrine' or 'beautiful night' depending on kanji. Also a modern Western name.
Nia: Welsh form of Niamh 'bright', Swahili 'purpose', or a short form of Antonia. Several unrelated origins.
Mill: Rare; probably a short form of Wilhelm or Miller, or the English word 'mill'. Origin uncertain.
Nilo: Spanish and Italian form of Nile, the river. Possibly from Greek Neilos. Meaning uncertain.
Orion: Greek, a hunter turned constellation. Origin of the name is uncertain.
Kataleya: Modern variant of Cattleya, an orchid genus named after William Cattley. Rare given name.
Bowie: Scottish, from a surname perhaps meaning 'yellow-haired' from Gaelic buidhe. Popularized by David Bowie.
Elyano: Modern coinage, probably blending Eli and Liano or Elian. Origin uncertain.
Lien: Dutch short form of names like Karolien or Marlien. Also Vietnamese 'lotus'.
Gianni: Italian short form of Giovanni, from Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Tibe: Dutch and Frisian variant of Tiebe, from the Germanic root 'people'. Origin somewhat uncertain.
Dilara: Persian and Turkish, meaning 'heart-adorning' or 'beloved'. From dil 'heart'.
Eve: Hebrew Chavah, meaning 'life' or 'living'. The first woman in the Bible.
Louca: Variant of Luca, the Italian form of Luke, from Greek 'man from Lucania'.
Merlin: Welsh Myrddin, the wizard of Arthurian legend, possibly from a place name 'sea fortress'. Also means 'falcon' in English.
Mayron: Probably a variant of Myron, from Greek myron 'fragrant oil'. Origin uncertain.
Elissa: Variant of Alyssa or Elisa; Elissa is also the Phoenician name of Dido. Meaning uncertain.
Eslem: Turkish; probably related to Arabic aslam 'safer, more peaceful'. Modern coinage, origin uncertain.
Joëlle: French feminine of Joel, from Hebrew 'Yahweh is God'.
Malou: Dutch and French blend of Maria and Louise, or Marie-Louise.
Eleonore: German and Scandinavian form of Eleanor, of uncertain origin. Possibly from Helen.
Billy: English diminutive of William, from Germanic 'will' and 'helmet'.
Yade: Probably Turkish, from yade 'jade'. Origin uncertain.
Santino: Italian diminutive of Santo, from Latin sanctus, meaning 'holy' or 'saint'.
Ianis: Variant of Yannis or Ioannis, forms of John, from Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Aïssatou: West African (Fula) form of Aisha, from Arabic 'alive' or 'living'.
Loena: Dutch coinage, from Luna, Latin for 'moon'. Variant of Luna.
Aida: Arabic 'visitor' or 'returning'. Also the name of Verdi's opera heroine.
Fonne: Dutch and Flemish short form of Alfons or Fons, from Germanic 'noble and ready'.
Anir: Probably Arabic 'luminous' or 'radiant', a variant of Anwar. Origin uncertain.
Bella: Italian, meaning 'beautiful'. Also a short form of Isabella.
Sofía: Spanish form of Sophia, from Greek sophia, meaning 'wisdom'.
Aram: Armenian, a legendary patriarch. Also Hebrew 'exalted'. Origin uncertain.
Polly: English diminutive of Molly, a form of Mary, from Hebrew, of uncertain meaning.
Diaz: Spanish patronymic, originally 'son of Diego'. Rare as a given name.
Ubbe: Old Norse and Frisian, a short form of names beginning with Ub-. Origin uncertain.
Elyo: Modern name, probably a variant of Elio or Elijah. Elio is from Greek helios, 'sun'.
Morgane: French form of Morgan, from Welsh meaning 'sea-born' or 'sea circle'. Morgan le Fay in Arthurian legend.
Kyara: Modern name; possibly from Japanese kyara 'agarwood' or a spelling of Kiara or Clara. Origin uncertain.
Zita: Italian dialect word for 'girl', or from Greek 'seeker'. Borne by Saint Zita and Empress Zita.
Nisrine: Arabic Nisrin, meaning 'wild rose' or 'dog rose'.
Laurence: French form of Laurentius, meaning 'from Laurentum' or 'laurel'. Used for both sexes in French.
Len: Short form of Leonard, from Germanic 'brave lion', or Dutch short form of Leander.
Ruth: Hebrew, possibly meaning 'friend' or 'compassion'. A biblical book about a loyal daughter-in-law.
Melisa: Turkish and Spanish form of Melissa, from Greek 'honey bee'.
Yohan: French form of Johan, from Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Cisse: West African surname, widely used as a given name; possibly Mande origin. Also a Dutch short form of Cecilia.
Ismaïl: Arabic form of Ishmael, from Hebrew 'God hears'.
Alana: Possibly Celtic, from Irish 'little rock' or 'fair', or feminine of Alan. Also Hawaiian 'awakening'. Origin uncertain.
Fatma: Turkish and Arabic form of Fatima, meaning 'one who abstains' or 'weaning'.
Hira: Arabic, referring to the cave of Hira where Muhammad received revelations. Also Hindi 'diamond'.
Lyne: Variant of Lynn, from Welsh llyn 'lake', or a short form of Caroline or Marilyne.
Elly: Dutch and English short form of Elisabeth, Eleanor or Helen.
Senna: Dutch, probably a variant of Sena or from the plant name senna, from Arabic. Origin uncertain.
Anatole: French form of Greek Anatolios, meaning 'sunrise' or 'east'.
Camelia: Latin, from the camellia flower named after Georg Kamel, a Jesuit botanist.
Safouane: Variant spelling of Arabic Safwan, meaning 'clear' or 'pure'.
Iza: Polish short form of Izabela, from Hebrew 'God is my oath'.
Elea: Probably a variant of Eleanor or Greek Elea, an ancient city of Italy. Origin uncertain.
Mirza: Persian, from Amirzada, meaning 'prince'. Used as a title and given name in the Balkans.
Louiza: Variant of Louisa, feminine of Louis, from Germanic 'famous warrior'.
Sia: Probably Swahili or Sanskrit-linked; also a short form of Sophia or Asia. Origin uncertain.
Atilla: Hungarian form of Attila, Gothic 'little father'. The famous Hun king.
Cezar: Romanian and Polish form of Caesar, the Roman title. Origin possibly 'hairy' or 'cut'.
Suleyman: Turkish form of Solomon, from Hebrew shalom, meaning 'peace'.
Frida: Scandinavian and German short form of names with Germanic frid 'peace'. Borne by Frida Kahlo.
Alfred: Old English Ælfræd, from ælf 'elf' and ræd 'counsel'. Borne by Alfred the Great.
Lev: Russian and Hebrew, meaning 'lion' in Russian and 'heart' in Hebrew.
Attilio: Italian form of Latin Attilius, a Roman family name, possibly a diminutive of Atta 'father'.
Violet: English, from the flower, ultimately Latin viola.
Noël: French, meaning 'Christmas', from Latin natalis 'birth'. Given to children born at Christmas.
Esmé: French, meaning 'esteemed' or 'beloved'. From Old French esmer 'to esteem'.
Amaël: Probably a Breton or Hebrew-inspired name. Possibly a variant of Amaury or 'work of God'. Origin uncertain.
Karan: Sanskrit, meaning 'ear', hence 'one who listens'. Also an epic figure, Karna.
Imrân: Arabic Imran, the father of Mary in the Quran. Probably from Hebrew Amram, meaning 'exalted people'.
Efnan: Turkish, possibly from Arabic afnan 'branches'. Rare; origin uncertain.
Wateen: Arabic, possibly from watin, meaning 'jugular vein' or 'lifeline'. Rare; sense uncertain.
Arne: Scandinavian and Dutch, from Old Norse Arni, meaning 'eagle'.
Toon: Dutch short form of Antoon (Anthony), from the Roman family name Antonius.
Cato: Latin cato, meaning 'wise' or 'sharp'. In Flanders also a short form of Catharina.
Leen: Dutch short form of Helena or Magdalena. Also Arabic 'tenderness' or 'softness'.
Niel: Dutch short form of Daniël or Cornelis, or variant of Neil, from Gaelic 'champion'.
Giulian: Variant of Julian, from Latin Julianus, derived from the family name Julius.
Kyle: Scottish, from Gaelic caol 'narrow strait'. Also from an English place name.
Vincenzo: Italian form of Vincent, from Latin vincere, meaning 'to conquer'.
Felien: Dutch and Flemish, probably a variant of Felicia or Felicien, from Latin 'happy, fortunate'.
Jacques: French form of James or Jacob, from Hebrew Yaakov, usually explained as 'supplanter'.
Adnan: Arabic, meaning 'settler'. An ancestor of the Adnanite Arabs.
Wael: Arabic, meaning 'one who seeks refuge' or 'returning to safety'.
Renee: English form of Renée, from French 'reborn', from Latin renatus.
Aurelie: Variant of French Aurélie, meaning 'golden', from Latin aureus.
Waïl: French spelling of Arabic Wael, meaning 'one who seeks refuge'.
Ikra: Variant of Iqra, Arabic for 'read' or 'recite', the first word revealed in the Quran.
Amadeo: Spanish and Italian form of Amadeus, from Latin, meaning 'love of God'.
Abdoul: French spelling of Abdul, Arabic 'servant of the', as in Abdoul Karim.
Sajid: Arabic, meaning 'one who prostrates in worship'.
Rinus: Dutch short form of Marinus or Reinier, from Latin marinus 'of the sea'.
Hadja: West African and Arabic, from hajja, a woman who has made the pilgrimage to Mecca.
Penelope: Greek, possibly from pene 'thread' or 'duck'. The faithful wife of Odysseus.
Celle: Rare; probably a Dutch short form of Marcel or a variant of Cel. Origin uncertain.
Eliam: Hebrew, meaning 'God of the people'. Biblical name, also a modern spelling of Elian.
Lua: Portuguese, meaning 'moon'. Also used as a Polynesian name.
Melania: Greek, meaning 'black' or 'dark'. Borne by Saint Melania.
Tillie: English diminutive of Matilda, from Germanic 'strength in battle'.
Thijs: Dutch short form of Matthijs, the Dutch form of Matthew, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Matthieu: French form of Matthew, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Dounia: Arabic Dunya, meaning 'world' or 'life'. Maghrebi spelling.
Tijl: Dutch, known from Tijl Uilenspiegel, the trickster. Likely a short form of Dietrich, Germanic 'people-ruler'.
Zeno: Greek, probably from Zeus, meaning 'of Zeus'. Borne by the Stoic philosopher Zeno.
Erika: Feminine of Erik, from Old Norse 'eternal ruler'. Also German for 'heather'.
Anouar: Arabic Anwar, meaning 'brighter' or 'more luminous'. French spelling.
Amel: Arabic, meaning 'hope'. Also a Bosnian name.
Rana: Arabic, meaning 'gazing' or 'eye-catching'. Also Sanskrit 'king' and Hindi 'royal'.
Alejandro: Spanish form of Alexander, from Greek 'defender of men'.
Mario: Italian and Spanish, from Roman family name Marius, possibly related to Mars.
Esila: Turkish, possibly a modern coinage meaning 'wise, lovely'. Origin uncertain.
Nola: Possibly Irish, a short form of Fionnuala, 'white shoulder'. Also from Latin 'bell'. Origin uncertain.
Anais: Occitan and French form of Anna or Hannah, Hebrew 'grace'. Spelled Anaïs in French.
Collin: English, from a short form of Nicholas or from a Gaelic surname. Nicholas is Greek 'victory of the people'.
Eppo: Frisian, probably from a short form of Germanic names with ebur 'boar'. Rare; origin uncertain.
Islam: Arabic, meaning 'submission' or 'peace'. Used as a given name in the Muslim world.
Haris: Arabic Haris, meaning 'guardian' or 'protector'. Also Greek Charis, 'grace'.
Arian: Albanian and Welsh; Welsh arian means 'silver'. In Persian, from Aryan 'noble'.
Nestor: Greek, possibly 'one who returns home'. The wise old king in the Iliad.
Naila: Arabic, meaning 'one who attains' or 'acquirer'. Also Swahili.
Theodor: German form of Theodore, from Greek 'gift of God'.
Saif: Arabic, meaning 'sword'. Used in names like Saif al-Din.
Luís: Portuguese form of Louis, from Germanic 'famous warrior'.
Ise: Probably a Dutch or Frisian short form of Isabel or Ida. Also a Japanese place name. Origin uncertain.
Asher: Hebrew, meaning 'happy' or 'blessed'. A son of Jacob.
Taim: Arabic, meaning 'enslaved by love' or 'devoted'. Rare; sometimes spelled Taym.
Lyra: Greek and Latin, the musical instrument and a constellation. Meaning 'lyre'.
Thélyo: Modern coinage, possibly from Greek thelo 'to wish' or a blend of Théo and Elio. Origin uncertain.
Sézane: Modern French name, perhaps from Cézanne or the French fashion brand. Origin uncertain; probably coined.
Artem: Ukrainian and Russian form of Artemios, from Greek, possibly 'of Artemis'.
Bram: Dutch short form of Abraham, from Hebrew 'father of many'.
Gaëlle: Breton, feminine of Gaël, meaning 'Gaul' or 'Gael'. Possibly from Breton gael, 'generous'.
Ashley: English, from a surname meaning 'ash tree clearing'. Used for both sexes.
Igor: Russian form of Ingvar, from Old Norse, meaning 'Yngvi's warrior'.
Ahmet: Turkish form of Ahmad, meaning 'most praised', from the same Arabic root as Muhammad.
Jamie: Scottish diminutive of James, from Hebrew Yaakov. Used for both sexes.
Nadir: Arabic, meaning 'rare' or 'precious'. Also English 'lowest point'.
Leni: German short form of Helene or Magdalene.
Eleni: Greek form of Helen, usually explained as 'torch' or 'shining light'.
Guust: Flemish short form of Gustaaf (Gustav), from Swedish 'staff of the Goths'.
Molly: English diminutive of Mary, from Hebrew, of uncertain meaning.
Aïsha: Arabic Aisha, meaning 'alive' or 'living'. The Prophet Muhammad's wife.
Laila: Arabic Layla, meaning 'night'. A tragic heroine of classical Arabic poetry.
Lizzy: English diminutive of Elizabeth, from Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Tasnime: French spelling of Arabic Tasnim, a spring in paradise. From the root meaning 'to raise'.
Juliet: English form of Juliette, a French diminutive of Julia, from the Roman family name Julius.
Mael: Breton and Welsh, meaning 'prince' or 'chief'. Also a Breton saint.
Lot: Dutch short form of Charlotte. Also Hebrew 'veil' as the biblical nephew of Abraham.
Thalya: Variant of Thalia, from Greek, meaning 'to blossom'. The muse of comedy.
Nil: Turkish and Catalan form of Nile or Nicholas. In Turkish, meaning 'indigo'.
Lois: Greek, of uncertain origin; possibly meaning 'better' or 'desirable'. Biblical grandmother of Timothy.
Fré: Flemish short form of Frederik or Frans, from Germanic 'peaceful ruler'.
Austin: English, a medieval form of Augustine, from Latin augustus 'venerable'.
Almira: Spanish and Arabic, from Arabic al-amira, meaning 'the princess'.
Saul: Hebrew, meaning 'asked for' or 'prayed for'. The first king of Israel.
Ewen: Breton and Scottish, a form of Eoghan or Yves, perhaps 'born of the yew'.
Naïa: Modern name, perhaps from Greek naias 'water nymph'. Origin uncertain.
Maëlya: Modern French blend of Maël and Lya. Origin uncertain.
Amélya: Modern variant of Amelia, from Germanic amal 'work'.
Edgard: French form of Edgar, from Old English ead 'wealth' and gar 'spear'.
Silya: Modern variant of Silia or Celia. Origin uncertain.
Alyana: Modern coinage, probably blending Aliyah and Ana. Origin uncertain.
Lamine: West African, from Arabic Amin, meaning 'trustworthy'. Often used with the article al-.
Medeea: Romanian form of Medea, from Greek, meaning 'cunning' or 'ruler'.
Vanessa: Invented by Jonathan Swift from Esther Vanhomrigh's name. Later a butterfly genus.
Sabrina: Latin, the name of the River Severn. A nymph in Welsh legend.
Antonin: French and Czech form of Antoninus, from the Roman family name Antonius.
